Area.evidence_source: This study suggests there is a group of high-risk individuals with no previous attempts who need to be identified and engaged with. In summary, prevention efforts may need to be directed both at those who exhibit low mastery and histories of multiple failed attempts, and at those with no previous attempts, who may be more determined and efficacious. Previous research has suggested those who have attempted suicide desire immediate and sometimes longer term community-based support, both in groups or one to one (Hume and Platt 2007). This package may best be coordinated by the voluntary sector and staffed by practitioners who are willing to show the patience and respect that are needed in order to engage with this group, whose lack of trust in the system makes them reluctant help seekers (Howerton et al. 2007).
